question: Which model can you use to generate text from speech?
explanation: Generating text from speech is speech transcription (speech-to-text): you submit audio and the model returns a text transcript. In Microsoft Foundry the speech-to-text models of the gpt-4o family carry the `-transcribe` suffix: gpt-4o-transcribe, gpt-4o-mini-transcribe and gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize. You call them with `client.audio.transcriptions.create()` on the `AzureOpenAI` client of the OpenAI SDK.

addition: Plain gpt-4o-mini is a chat model for text and image processing, not a speech model. Audio in that family comes from the `-transcribe` and `-tts` models and from previews such as gpt-4o-mini-audio-preview and gpt-4o-mini-realtime-preview.

question: Which model can you use to synthesize speech from text?
explanation: Speech synthesis (text-to-speech) is the reverse of speech-to-text: you submit text and the model returns an audio stream of the vocalized text. In Microsoft Foundry the text-to-speech models of the gpt-4o family carry the `-tts` suffix: gpt-4o-tts and gpt-4o-mini-tts. You call them with `client.audio.speech.with_streaming_response.create()`, passing a `voice`, the `input` text and optional `instructions` for the tone.
